elements.element: Vendor expressly indemnifies Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) states that TrueLink shall indemnify Client against specified third-party IP claims.

elements.element: Vendor expressly defends Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause requires indemnification but contains no express duty to defend.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer's affiliates against the covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Although Section 12(b) names Client's affiliates for breach-related claims, the new IP indemnity in Section 12(c) protects only Client, and the other preferred claim categories are absent.

elements.element: Vendor defends Customer's affiliates against the covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: No duty to defend is stated, and Section 12(c) does not name Client's affiliates.

elements.element: Covered claims include third-party allegations that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) covers third-party claims that the Interface, Hosting Services, or Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Covered claims include third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No express Vendor indemnity for claims arising from TrueLink's violation or breach of law is included.

elements.element: Covered claims include third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no data-breach indemnity or causation trigger tied to TrueLink.

elements.element: Covered claims include third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence and wilful misconduct are not stated as indemnity triggers.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires Customer to give Vendor notice of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No notice procedure appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure gives Vendor control of the defense and settlement of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No defense or settlement-control provision appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires Customer to provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Customer indemnifies Vendor for claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Section 12(a)(iii) covers claims arising from or relating to Client Content, including content posted by Client and its personnel or authorized customers.

elements.element: Customer indemnifies Vendor for claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 12(a)(ii) covers claims resulting from relevant Client acts or omissions constituting a violation of state or federal law, rule, or regulation.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity is limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 12(a) additionally covers any Client breach of the Agreement, acts causing TrueLink defaults under third-party agreements, claims relating broadly to the Web Site, and product-, service-, or information-related personal injury and property damage.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims concerning the services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) expressly indemnifies Client against third-party claims that the Interface, Hosting Services, or Support Services infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims arising from Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) excludes claims to the extent arising from modifications made by Client.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims arising from Customer combinations with items not supplied by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) excludes claims arising from Client's combination of the covered items with items not supplied by TrueLink.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims arising from Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) expressly excludes claims arising from Client's specifications.

elements.element: The IP remedies include procuring Customer's right to continue using the affected item.
elements.evidence: TrueLink must procure for Client the right to continue use of the affected item as one remedial option.

elements.element: The IP remedies include modifying the affected item to make it non-infringing.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) includes modification so the affected item is non-infringing.

elements.element: The IP remedies include replacing the affected item with a non-infringing equivalent.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) includes replacement with a non-infringing equivalent.

elements.element: The IP remedies include refunding fees if procurement, modification, and replacement are unavailable.
elements.evidence: If none of the preceding remedies is available, TrueLink must refund the fees paid for the affected item.

elements.element: Vendor's liability for the IP indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) caps TrueLink's total liability under that subsection at 3x the annual fees paid by Client under the Agreement.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the fallback IP indemnity, exclusions, remedy sequence, and 3x annual-fees cap while otherwise leaving the parties' indemnities intact. It does not satisfy the preferred position because it omits an express defense duty, protection of affiliates under the IP clause, Vendor breach-of-law, data-breach, and gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct triggers, and all standard indemnification procedures. It also leaves Client's indemnity substantially broader than the preferred two permitted categories.
